newsitem.title: USA: Pioneer Railcorp Q1 carloadings up 26 pct.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer Railcorp Q1 carloadings up 26 pct.

text.p: Pioneer Railcorp, a short line railroad holding company, said Tuesday that carloadings in the 1997 first quarter rose 26 percent over the same period a year ago.
Pioneer's first quarter carloadings increased to 8,475 from 6,734 in the same quarter in 1996.
Carloadings shipped is one of the factors used in determining Pioneer's gross revenues.
Freight railroads acquired by Pioneer during the past year accounted for more than 40 percent of the first quarter carloadings total, Pioneer noted.
In March, Pioneer carloadings shipped rose 10 percent over last year, with 2,921 versus 2,634.

"The reopening of a strategic bridge, more moderate weather and recent increases in lumber, grain and steel production by our customers should contribute to our growth this year," said Guy Brenkman, Pioneer's chairman and chief executive officer, in a statement.
Pioneer operates 15 freight short line railroads with over 500 miles of track in nine states. It owns about 900 rail cars and locomotives.
